# A query's @load reads the loop variable it was written under, on every
# target.
#
# A new kind hands each copy's query a new word. On the instance runtimes the
# render hands a kept instance its props one at a time, each setter settling
# it: the new key mounted, the fetch answered at once, and the @load the last
# render handed over ran, writing under the last word. A function prop is now
# handed over first. bubbletea splices the query per copy and runs its
# handlers from the settle, outside the loop, which refused the read of `w`;
# the handler now binds it from the copy's key.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import async "sngl:async"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

// A word as a lookup answers it, at once: itself, marked.
func lookUp(word string) async.Result[string] {
    return {ok="{word}!"}
}

component page ui.node {
    var kind = "Red"
    var seen map[string, string] = {}

    ui.vbox {
        for var w = ["{kind}-a", "{kind}-b"] {
            async.query(on=w, fetch=lookUp, @load(got) { seen[w] = got })
        }
        ui.button #next(text="next", @click { kind = "Green" })
    }
}

ui.window {
    page()
}

func testEachAnswerLandsUnderItsWord(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.assert(c.seen.get("Red-a", "") == "Red-a!")
    c.next.click()
    t.wait(func() => c.seen.length() == 4, 2000)
    t.assert(c.seen.get("Green-a", "") == "Green-a!")
    t.assert(c.seen.get("Green-b", "") == "Green-b!")
}
